## Motivation This is the second pass of #44690. Three weeks after that PR, `python/sglang/kernels` had gained another 66K lines, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen` 43K and `test/registered` 162K. This PR removes what in that code is dead or redundant. More importantly, it fixes the places where CI is green without testing anything, and the runtime bugs found along the way. **433 files, +5,551 / −13,052.** - About 1.4K of the additions are tests moved to `test/manual/`, because no CI runner has the hardware or package they need. - About 0.8K are shared test helpers that replace copies. ## Bugs fixed (please review these first) | Area | Problem | Fix | |---|---|---| | Kernel CI | `base-b-kernel-unit-test-8-gpu-h200` has no registered test. On every kernel PR and three times a day it books an 8×H200 runner, installs everything, and logs `No tests found`. | Matrix row and suite removed. | | Kernel CI | Tests registered on lanes whose hardware never satisfies their skip gate. The production kernels behind them had no CI at all. | Registered on hardware that runs them, and each was run there:
• SM120 FlashMLA fallback (`Ran 15; skipped=15` on H100)
• Blackwell FP4 indexer quant (36 of 39 cases skipped)
• Q8KV8 sparse prefill (25 cases)
• FlashInfer KDA prefill graph and input pack
• SM100 Mamba stochastic rounding
• the FA3 extend-init regression
• KDA MTP slot stride
• Gemma4 Blackwell sampling split
• gfx950-only kernels on the MI300 lane
• diffusion FA4 `forward_into`
• SubBlock sm100/sm120 kernels (one case skipped on sm_100, see below)
• 4-rank and 2-rank diffusion cases on 1-GPU lanes | | Q8KV8 sparse prefill | Once the Blackwell cases ran, 15 of them failed on main. #45909 packed each request's compressed history contiguously and updated the H100 cases, but nobody ran the Blackwell cases, so their expected offsets stayed stale. Their output-vs-paged-attention assertion passes. | Registration and expectation fix land together; 37 passed on sm_103. | | Kernel tests | `test_kpool_topk_transform_fused.py` runs under `unittest.main()`, which drops the module-level pytest functions. 4 of its cases (ties, overfull bins, page-table mapping under graph replay) never ran. | `pytest.main` entry; scanned the kernel tests for the same pattern. | | Kernel tests | Assertions that cannot fail:
• a tensor compared with itself (`test_rmsnorm`);
• an AMD all-reduce "determinism" test with no assert, which only prints ✓/✗ and tests RCCL rather than SGLang;
• `*_jit_vs_aot` comparisons against AOT ops that do not exist (always skipped);
• a MoE wna16 GEMM test that always skipped (it now checks against a dequant reference and runs its 24 cases). | Fixed, or deleted where nothing SGLang-owned was tested. | | Unit tests | Triton kernels tested only from CPU-registered files, so their CUDA cases never ran: `row_logsumexp[_topk]`, `free_unbind_inplace`, `gather_page64_kv_latent`, the token-id translation Triton path. | GPU registrations added (5090). | | Unit tests | Tests of copies of the code instead of the code:
• the decode CUDA-graph profile options (a test-local copy);
• four MoE shared-expert fusion gates asserting only `assertTrue(reason)`, which the CPU early-return satisfies;
• `test_h3_request.py`, which failed 8 of 12 cases when run alone because its ComfyUI stubs had rotted. It passed only if another test happened to import the real module first. | The tests now call the real method and assert each branch's message. The stubs are fixed. | | CI registration | `test_gated_launch.py` used `nightly=True` on a CUDA registration, so no job ever ran it. | Flag removed; it now runs in nightly. `check_registered_tests.py` rejects `nightly=True` on CUDA/CPU. | | CI tooling | `update_est_time.py` matched registrations with a single-line regex. It missed 150 of the 2,459 CUDA/CPU registrations (wrapped, positional, float), so their `est_time` never refreshed. | The literal is found through the AST: 0 missed. | | Diffusion | `--srt-encoder-connection-timeout` was stored under a name that is not a field, so the documented flag (and the one GLM-Image's timeout error recommends) was silently dropped. `type=int` also rejected the documented default 3.05. | `dest=` the field, `type=float`. | | Diffusion VMoBA | The runtime imported `kernel.attn.vmoba_attn.vmoba`, which exists nowhere. The chunk-selection fix in #44286 went into the in-tree copy that nothing imported, and its tests sat outside CI discovery. | The runtime and resolver import the in-tree module. Its tests moved into `multimodal_gen/test/unit`. | | Diffusion `exact` tier | Wan and LingBot fuse Q/K/V into one GEMM unconditionally. At the model shapes it is bit-identical on H200 and GB300. At M ≤ 256, cuBLAS picks split-K and the result differs, so `exact` requests were not bit-identical. Wan's fused RMSNorm+RoPE had no check either. | The QKV fusion is gated at `lossless` (same math, rounding moves), the default tier, so default behavior is unchanged. The norm+RoPE fusion goes through `BitExactFusionGate.run`. | | MiniMax-H3 | The pipelined Ulysses attention never ran its first-call equality check. Enabling the check exposed that the sequential reference left non-zero pad rows that #47566 zeroes, which would have turned the pipeline off. | The reference zeroes the alignment rows (never read downstream); the check runs and passes (`same=1`). | | Registry | `gemm.dsv3_fused_a_gemm` pointed at `sgl_kernel:dsv3_fused_a_gemm`, which does not exist. The namespace test only checked that the module existed. | Spec removed. `test_inventory_targets_resolve` now resolves every target's attribute statically (incl. the AOT package) on the CPU lane. | | CuTe DSL GDN/KDA decode | The wrappers accepted `scale`, `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel`, `softplus_beta` and `softplus_threshold`, then compiled with fixed values. Today's callers pass exactly those values. | Non-matching values raise `ValueError` (+ test). | | ROCm block-FP8 | `use_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_unrolledx4` evaluated its condition without `return`, so production never selected the unrolledx4 kernel. Only the tuner ran it. | Kernel, selector and tuner branch removed. Runtime behavior is unchanged. | | Unlimited-OCR / QK-norm gate | Their PDL probes checked `capability >= 9`, which is true on gfx942/950, so they emitted PDL on ROCm. | `current_arch().supports_pdl`. | ## Modifications ### Kernels (`python/sglang/kernels`, 108 files, −3.1K net) - **Dead code** (each re-checked by whole-repo grep, incl. string targets): - 865 lines of `jit/csrc/moe/expert_specialization/*.cuh` that nothing loads; - ngram decode fast paths that were never wired in, and their benchmarks; - the MuseSpark `router_gemm` JIT kernel (the model only uses its token limit); - the test-only TextSeal standalone selector; - two unused LoRA MoE custom ops; - LPLB shmem helpers, `row_argmax` and `create_argmax_workspace`; - the f32x2 helpers left by a reverted PR; - `finish_flat_indexer_topk`; - the `small_field_copy` descriptor path; - an unloadable LoRA plans table; - losing `mla_qk_prep` variants (the default path is byte-identical on H200 and GB300 over 64 cases); - unused `use_tma`/`topk`/`config` parameters; - the MuseSpark softmax routing branches; - aliases, constants and re-exports nothing uses. - **Classification** (#45112 rules): - `engram_gather_peer` (peer-memory read) → `communication`. - MSA-v1 `compact_dequant` (KV-cache gather + dequant) → `kvcache`. - The two diffusion op ids that targeted quantization/activation modules are renamed to their real groups; their facade re-exports are gone. - `qwen_moe_topk_output` moves to its only caller in `qwen2_moe.py`. - The gfx1250 per-token FP8 quant → `quantization`. - **Arch queries:** about 15 sites that still probed the device by hand now use `sglang.kernels.arch` (#47782) with the same semantics. `argmax`/`softmax` JIT adopt `max_vec_bytes`. Import-time device-0 probes moved to call time. - **Dedups:** - the gfx950 gluon MoE helpers (identical AMDGCN for all 68 cases); - the hipcc compile-and-load block; - the SM90 FP8 CuTeDSL LoRA class, now a subclass of its BF16 sibling (bit-exact on H200); - the gfx950 vattn HIP binding. - **Env:** raw `os.environ` reads in kernels/models are declared in `environ.py` with the same names and defaults. Two settings are removed: - `SGLANG_HIP_MHC_BOUNDARY_WIDE_TILE`, a kill switch for a bitwise-identical tile; - `SGLANG_XPU_LN_MOD_NUM_WARPS`, a layout-only setting. - **HiCache:** the page-unified layout is admitted only if both the write-back and the load-back JIT probes pass; until now the load-back probe was never called. - **Docs:** cookbook lines that told users to set env vars nothing reads are removed. ### Diffusion (`python/sglang/multimodal_gen`, 118 files, −1.5K net) - **Dead code:** - 7 disaggregation flags nothing read; - `--mask-strategy-file-path` (sliding-tile attention reads `--attention-backend-config mask_strategy_file_path=...`, and the error now says so); - the `/stats` timeout counter that was always 0; - vestigial `PortArgs` fields that leaked three temp files per construction; - about 25 unused helpers, constants and config fields; - test oracles moved out of runtime modules into the tests. - **Shared helpers:** - four more hand-written verify-once gates use `BitExactFusionGate.run` / `can_attempt` (flux3 video VAE, FLUX.2 XPU, KL-VAE, Qwen-Image-2.1); - Wan and LingBot share one row-packing helper; - the duplicated Nomas helpers, OpenAI image/video/mesh API helpers and flux3's copy of the launcher conditions are merged; - the two disagreeing "unrecoverable device error" classifiers are now one. - **Docs:** - `--enable-attention-backend-autotune` was documented but not a CLI flag; it is now one. - `ring_sp_performance.mdx` documented a flag that does not exist; it now uses the real `--kv-gather-degree`. ### Tests and CI - **Deleted:** - tautologies (argparse pass-through, default and constant echoes, `inspect.getsource`/AST source tests, mock-the-SUT, torch-math); - duplicate cases and files; - benchmarks of test-local copies; - always-skipped tests; - `#47603` leftovers (dead model lists, a test that `return`s in CI); - tests with a hard-coded developer path. - **Merged** copy-pasted fakes, fixtures and oracles into `python/sglang/test/` helpers. Two test classes were collected twice through imports (45 extra runs per CPU job). - **Trimmed grids** with no coverage gain: page-unified dtype sweep (252 → 168 cases), MiniMax decode top-k (144 → 48). - **Faster CPU gate:** - `test_runtime_context.py`: 132 s → 13 s; - `test_flashinfer_autotune_sync.py`: 30 s → 10 s; - three one-purpose files merged. - **Moved to `test/manual/`:** tests that need NCCL ≥ 2.31.2, a private checkpoint, an unset env var, or 4 GPUs of a manual-only class; plus a benchmark CLI that lived in a registered test. - **CI:** - the empty 8-GPU XPU nightly job is removed; - stale suite names, globs and `rerun_test_groups` entries are removed; - the Muse Spark HF token follows the runner, not the stage; - `comfy-kitchen` (no deps) is installed for the diffusion unit/B200 jobs, so its three tests stop skipping. ## Behavior changes - Diffusion CLI: - the 7 unused disaggregation flags and `--mask-strategy-file-path` are now rejected; - `--srt-encoder-connection-timeout` takes effect and accepts floats. - Diffusion `exact` requests no longer use the fused QKV GEMM (Wan, LingBot). `lossless` and `high` outputs are byte-identical to main. - HiDream-O1 rejects `--flow-shift`/`--scheduler-class-override`, as it already does for its other fixed settings. HunyuanImage-3 honors a user `--flow-shift` instead of overwriting it. - `/v1/images/edits` returns 400 when `mask` is given; it was silently ignored. - The diffusion client treats `CUDA error:`, `HIP error:` and `torch.AcceleratorError` as unrecoverable, like the worker does. - ROCm: no PDL in the Unlimited-OCR DASH / QK-norm gate kernels. The gfx1250 kpool indexer uses Triton `act_quant`, like the other two DSA paths. - CuTe DSL LoRA prepare: SM120 now gets a clear `NotImplementedError` instead of compiling the SM100 class and failing. - Removed env vars: `SGLANG_HIP_MHC_BOUNDARY_WIDE_TILE`, `SGLANG_XPU_LN_MOD_NUM_WARPS`. Newly declared boolean envs (`SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_FP8_BS`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_LFM_FUSED_CONV`) parse like every other `EnvBool`. ## Left alone (owner decisions, not in this PR) - **AMD/NPU suites no workflow runs:** 55 AMD files (~8.9K lines) and 8 NPU files (~1.5K lines) register suites that no workflow invokes. `run_suite.py` does not validate AMD/NPU suite names. The list is in a comment below. - **Cake softmax on SM100:** since the JIT branch went first (#47512), the Cake softmax can no longer be selected; its input domain is inside the JIT one. - **MiniMax-H3 4-GPU H100 smoke suite:** `FILE_SUITES["4-gpu-h100"]` has no bridge file and no workflow, so its three cases never run. - **Code waiting on #46693:** the gfx950 kernels from #46690–#46692 that #46693 wires. - **Auto-residency probe:** unreachable since #45979 ("until a planner consumes it"). - **SubBlock ragged tail on sm_100:** `TestSubBlockNumerics::test_ragged_tail_reproduces_dense` returns NaN on the B200 lane and passes on sm_103 and sm_120. The kernel is not changed here, so the case is skipped on sm_100 until the tail path is fixed. - **`topk_sigmoid` on ROCm:** every case of `test_moe_topk_sigmoid.py` failed on the MI300 jit-kernel lane, so the test stays CUDA-only. - **`pr-test-sgl-kernel.yml` benchmark loop:** `|| echo` means the job cannot fail. ## Accuracy Tests **Full regression sweep, base (`4c7c775c`) vs this branch, same box.** Each test file runs in its own pytest process. Failing test ids are compared: | Box | Files | Test ids failing only on this branch | |---|---|---| | H200 (sm_90) | `test/registered/kernels/ops` (448), `test/registered/unit` (1153), `multimodal_gen/test/unit` (395) | **0** | | GB300 (sm_103) | `test/registered/kernels/ops` (448) | **0** (15 fewer: the Q8KV8 Blackwell cases) | | RTX 5090 (sm_120) | `test/registered/kernels/ops` (448) | **0** (the same 833 pre-existing ids) | The remaining failures are identical on both trees: multi-GPU tests on a 1-GPU box, optional packages missing from the image, and kernels that need hardware the box lacks. **End to end, fixed seed, base vs this branch.** An instrumented run confirmed the fused paths were active on both sides. | Model | Box | Result | |---|---|---| | Wan2.1-1.3B | H200 | `lossless`, `exact` and `high` mp4 byte-identical; fused QKV GEMM active (M=14040); norm+RoPE gate verified | | Wan2.1-14B | GB300 | `lossless` and `exact` byte-identical | | Qwen-Image-2.1 | H200 | byte-identical; 10 DiT gates verified (incl. the converted ones) | | LingBot-World realtime (CI case) | H200 | `exact` and `lossless` raw frames identical; fused GEMM active under `lossless` | | MiniMax-H3 T2VA, Ulysses 2 | GB300 | `lossless` and `exact` byte-identical; pipelined attention first-call check `same=1` | **Kernel dedups, bit-for-bit (`torch.equal` on dumped outputs, base vs branch):** - the CuTeDSL FP8 LoRA class merge, `gelu_and_mul_triton`, MuseSpark routing, argmax and the SM10x JIT softmax: 88 tensors on H200 and 112 on GB300; - `mla_qk_prep`: 64 cases on H200 and GB300; - the gfx950 gluon helper hoist: identical AMDGCN for all 68 cases (372 compiles via Triton's AMD backend). **Lane changes** were run on the hardware of their new lane: - SM120 cases on an RTX 5090; - SM100/SM103 cases on GB300; - H100-lane cases on H200; - the new 4-GPU diffusion cases on 4×GB300. **CI tooling:** - `pre-commit run --from-ref 4c7c775c` passes over the whole range, including the workflow checks. - `check_registered_tests.py` passes; on main it fails, naming the `nightly=True` file. - Suite selection was simulated with `run_suite.filter_tests`, and `compute_partitions.py` gives the same shard counts for pr-test, pr-test-extra, nightly and weekly. - `update_est_time.py` dry run: 1402 updates, up from 1372; the old 1372 keep their values. - The diffusion partition planner reports 0 missing estimates, and both newly scheduled 2-GPU files ran on 2×GB300. - An import walk over `sglang.{kernels,multimodal_gen,srt,test}` finds no new import failures. - After merging main `851642ad`, the 18 test files touched by the newly merged upstream commits pass on main and on this branch. **Not validated:** - true SM100 / B200 (no B200 machine was available; sm_103 stood in for every `major == 10` gate); - ROCm, NPU, XPU and MUSA (those changes are mechanical and import-checked); - the VMoBA CUDA path (FlashAttention 2 is not in the image); - FLUX.3 e2e (gated weights); - HiDream-O1, HunyuanImage-3 and Nomas e2e (unit tests only). ## Speed Tests and Profiling No perf-path changes intended: - Default-tier fused paths are unchanged. - The removed kernels and branches were not selected in production. - The `mla_qk_prep` default variant is byte-identical. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #41849319311](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41849319311) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #41849319083](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41849319083) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #41849319222](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41849319222) > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change. Use `/rerun-test` to run the tests your change touches, or copy this prompt for an agent: > > ```text > Find the registered tests this PR affects and run them with /rerun-test, following https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.agents/skills/rerun-test/SKILL.md > ```

These files register suites that no workflow runs, and none of them is run by path either. `run_suite.py` validates suite names only for CUDA/CPU (`_SUITE_CHECKED_BACKENDS`), so a misspelled or retired AMD/NPU suite never fails. Each file needs to be wired to a job or deleted. Once they are, the same suite-name check could cover AMD and NPU.

detail.body:
## Motivation This is the second pass of #44690. Three weeks after that PR, `python/sglang/kernels` had gained another 66K lines, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen` 43K and `test/registered` 162K. This PR removes what in that code is dead or redundant. More importantly, it fixes the places where CI is green without testing anything, and the runtime bugs found along the way. **433 files, +5,551 / −13,052.** - About 1.4K of the additions are tests moved to `test/manual/`, because no CI runner has the hardware or package they need. - About 0.8K are shared test helpers that replace copies. ## Bugs fixed (please review these first) | Area | Problem | Fix | |---|---|---| | Kernel CI | `base-b-kernel-unit-test-8-gpu-h200` has no registered test. On every kernel PR and three times a day it books an 8×H200 runner, installs everything, and logs `No tests found`. | Matrix row and suite removed. | | Kernel CI | Tests registered on lanes whose hardware never satisfies their skip gate. The production kernels behind them had no CI at all. | Registered on hardware that runs them, and each was run there:
• SM120 FlashMLA fallback (`Ran 15; skipped=15` on H100)
• Blackwell FP4 indexer quant (36 of 39 cases skipped)
• Q8KV8 sparse prefill (25 cases)
• FlashInfer KDA prefill graph and input pack
• SM100 Mamba stochastic rounding
• the FA3 extend-init regression
• KDA MTP slot stride
• Gemma4 Blackwell sampling split
• gfx950-only kernels on the MI300 lane
• diffusion FA4 `forward_into`
• SubBlock sm100/sm120 kernels (one case skipped on sm_100, see below)
• 4-rank and 2-rank diffusion cases on 1-GPU lanes | | Q8KV8 sparse prefill | Once the Blackwell cases ran, 15 of them failed on main. #45909 packed each request's compressed history contiguously and updated the H100 cases, but nobody ran the Blackwell cases, so their expected offsets stayed stale. Their output-vs-paged-attention assertion passes. | Registration and expectation fix land together; 37 passed on sm_103. | | Kernel tests | `test_kpool_topk_transform_fused.py` runs under `unittest.main()`, which drops the module-level pytest functions. 4 of its cases (ties, overfull bins, page-table mapping under graph replay) never ran. | `pytest.main` entry; scanned the kernel tests for the same pattern. | | Kernel tests | Assertions that cannot fail:
• a tensor compared with itself (`test_rmsnorm`);
• an AMD all-reduce "determinism" test with no assert, which only prints ✓/✗ and tests RCCL rather than SGLang;
• `*_jit_vs_aot` comparisons against AOT ops that do not exist (always skipped);
• a MoE wna16 GEMM test that always skipped (it now checks against a dequant reference and runs its 24 cases). | Fixed, or deleted where nothing SGLang-owned was tested. | | Unit tests | Triton kernels tested only from CPU-registered files, so their CUDA cases never ran: `row_logsumexp[_topk]`, `free_unbind_inplace`, `gather_page64_kv_latent`, the token-id translation Triton path. | GPU registrations added (5090). | | Unit tests | Tests of copies of the code instead of the code:
• the decode CUDA-graph profile options (a test-local copy);
• four MoE shared-expert fusion gates asserting only `assertTrue(reason)`, which the CPU early-return satisfies;
• `test_h3_request.py`, which failed 8 of 12 cases when run alone because its ComfyUI stubs had rotted. It passed only if another test happened to import the real module first. | The tests now call the real method and assert each branch's message. The stubs are fixed. | | CI registration | `test_gated_launch.py` used `nightly=True` on a CUDA registration, so no job ever ran it. | Flag removed; it now runs in nightly. `check_registered_tests.py` rejects `nightly=True` on CUDA/CPU. | | CI tooling | `update_est_time.py` matched registrations with a single-line regex. It missed 150 of the 2,459 CUDA/CPU registrations (wrapped, positional, float), so their `est_time` never refreshed. | The literal is found through the AST: 0 missed. | | Diffusion | `--srt-encoder-connection-timeout` was stored under a name that is not a field, so the documented flag (and the one GLM-Image's timeout error recommends) was silently dropped. `type=int` also rejected the documented default 3.05. | `dest=` the field, `type=float`. | | Diffusion VMoBA | The runtime imported `kernel.attn.vmoba_attn.vmoba`, which exists nowhere. The chunk-selection fix in #44286 went into the in-tree copy that nothing imported, and its tests sat outside CI discovery. | The runtime and resolver import the in-tree module. Its tests moved into `multimodal_gen/test/unit`. | | Diffusion `exact` tier | Wan and LingBot fuse Q/K/V into one GEMM unconditionally. At the model shapes it is bit-identical on H200 and GB300. At M ≤ 256, cuBLAS picks split-K and the result differs, so `exact` requests were not bit-identical. Wan's fused RMSNorm+RoPE had no check either. | The QKV fusion is gated at `lossless` (same math, rounding moves), the default tier, so default behavior is unchanged. The norm+RoPE fusion goes through `BitExactFusionGate.run`. | | MiniMax-H3 | The pipelined Ulysses attention never ran its first-call equality check. Enabling the check exposed that the sequential reference left non-zero pad rows that #47566 zeroes, which would have turned the pipeline off. | The reference zeroes the alignment rows (never read downstream); the check runs and passes (`same=1`). | | Registry | `gemm.dsv3_fused_a_gemm` pointed at `sgl_kernel:dsv3_fused_a_gemm`, which does not exist. The namespace test only checked that the module existed. | Spec removed. `test_inventory_targets_resolve` now resolves every target's attribute statically (incl. the AOT package) on the CPU lane. | | CuTe DSL GDN/KDA decode | The wrappers accepted `scale`, `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel`, `softplus_beta` and `softplus_threshold`, then compiled with fixed values. Today's callers pass exactly those values. | Non-matching values raise `ValueError` (+ test). | | ROCm block-FP8 | `use_w8a8_block_fp8_matmul_unrolledx4` evaluated its condition without `return`, so production never selected the unrolledx4 kernel. Only the tuner ran it. | Kernel, selector and tuner branch removed. Runtime behavior is unchanged. | | Unlimited-OCR / QK-norm gate | Their PDL probes checked `capability >= 9`, which is true on gfx942/950, so they emitted PDL on ROCm. | `current_arch().supports_pdl`. | ## Modifications ### Kernels (`python/sglang/kernels`, 108 files, −3.1K net) - **Dead code** (each re-checked by whole-repo grep, incl. string targets): - 865 lines of `jit/csrc/moe/expert_specialization/*.cuh` that nothing loads; - ngram decode fast paths that were never wired in, and their benchmarks; - the MuseSpark `router_gemm` JIT kernel (the model only uses its token limit); - the test-only TextSeal standalone selector; - two unused LoRA MoE custom ops; - LPLB shmem helpers, `row_argmax` and `create_argmax_workspace`; - the f32x2 helpers left by a reverted PR; - `finish_flat_indexer_topk`; - the `small_field_copy` descriptor path; - an unloadable LoRA plans table; - losing `mla_qk_prep` variants (the default path is byte-identical on H200 and GB300 over 64 cases); - unused `use_tma`/`topk`/`config` parameters; - the MuseSpark softmax routing branches; - aliases, constants and re-exports nothing uses. - **Classification** (#45112 rules): - `engram_gather_peer` (peer-memory read) → `communication`. - MSA-v1 `compact_dequant` (KV-cache gather + dequant) → `kvcache`. - The two diffusion op ids that targeted quantization/activation modules are renamed to their real groups; their facade re-exports are gone. - `qwen_moe_topk_output` moves to its only caller in `qwen2_moe.py`. - The gfx1250 per-token FP8 quant → `quantization`. - **Arch queries:** about 15 sites that still probed the device by hand now use `sglang.kernels.arch` (#47782) with the same semantics. `argmax`/`softmax` JIT adopt `max_vec_bytes`. Import-time device-0 probes moved to call time. - **Dedups:** - the gfx950 gluon MoE helpers (identical AMDGCN for all 68 cases); - the hipcc compile-and-load block; - the SM90 FP8 CuTeDSL LoRA class, now a subclass of its BF16 sibling (bit-exact on H200); - the gfx950 vattn HIP binding. - **Env:** raw `os.environ` reads in kernels/models are declared in `environ.py` with the same names and defaults. Two settings are removed: - `SGLANG_HIP_MHC_BOUNDARY_WIDE_TILE`, a kill switch for a bitwise-identical tile; - `SGLANG_XPU_LN_MOD_NUM_WARPS`, a layout-only setting. - **HiCache:** the page-unified layout is admitted only if both the write-back and the load-back JIT probes pass; until now the load-back probe was never called. - **Docs:** cookbook lines that told users to set env vars nothing reads are removed. ### Diffusion (`python/sglang/multimodal_gen`, 118 files, −1.5K net) - **Dead code:** - 7 disaggregation flags nothing read; - `--mask-strategy-file-path` (sliding-tile attention reads `--attention-backend-config mask_strategy_file_path=...`, and the error now says so); - the `/stats` timeout counter that was always 0; - vestigial `PortArgs` fields that leaked three temp files per construction; - about 25 unused helpers, constants and config fields; - test oracles moved out of runtime modules into the tests. - **Shared helpers:** - four more hand-written verify-once gates use `BitExactFusionGate.run` / `can_attempt` (flux3 video VAE, FLUX.2 XPU, KL-VAE, Qwen-Image-2.1); - Wan and LingBot share one row-packing helper; - the duplicated Nomas helpers, OpenAI image/video/mesh API helpers and flux3's copy of the launcher conditions are merged; - the two disagreeing "unrecoverable device error" classifiers are now one. - **Docs:** - `--enable-attention-backend-autotune` was documented but not a CLI flag; it is now one. - `ring_sp_performance.mdx` documented a flag that does not exist; it now uses the real `--kv-gather-degree`. ### Tests and CI - **Deleted:** - tautologies (argparse pass-through, default and constant echoes, `inspect.getsource`/AST source tests, mock-the-SUT, torch-math); - duplicate cases and files; - benchmarks of test-local copies; - always-skipped tests; - `#47603` leftovers (dead model lists, a test that `return`s in CI); - tests with a hard-coded developer path. - **Merged** copy-pasted fakes, fixtures and oracles into `python/sglang/test/` helpers. Two test classes were collected twice through imports (45 extra runs per CPU job). - **Trimmed grids** with no coverage gain: page-unified dtype sweep (252 → 168 cases), MiniMax decode top-k (144 → 48). - **Faster CPU gate:** - `test_runtime_context.py`: 132 s → 13 s; - `test_flashinfer_autotune_sync.py`: 30 s → 10 s; - three one-purpose files merged. - **Moved to `test/manual/`:** tests that need NCCL ≥ 2.31.2, a private checkpoint, an unset env var, or 4 GPUs of a manual-only class; plus a benchmark CLI that lived in a registered test. - **CI:** - the empty 8-GPU XPU nightly job is removed; - stale suite names, globs and `rerun_test_groups` entries are removed; - the Muse Spark HF token follows the runner, not the stage; - `comfy-kitchen` (no deps) is installed for the diffusion unit/B200 jobs, so its three tests stop skipping. ## Behavior changes - Diffusion CLI: - the 7 unused disaggregation flags and `--mask-strategy-file-path` are now rejected; - `--srt-encoder-connection-timeout` takes effect and accepts floats. - Diffusion `exact` requests no longer use the fused QKV GEMM (Wan, LingBot). `lossless` and `high` outputs are byte-identical to main. - HiDream-O1 rejects `--flow-shift`/`--scheduler-class-override`, as it already does for its other fixed settings. HunyuanImage-3 honors a user `--flow-shift` instead of overwriting it. - `/v1/images/edits` returns 400 when `mask` is given; it was silently ignored. - The diffusion client treats `CUDA error:`, `HIP error:` and `torch.AcceleratorError` as unrecoverable, like the worker does. - ROCm: no PDL in the Unlimited-OCR DASH / QK-norm gate kernels. The gfx1250 kpool indexer uses Triton `act_quant`, like the other two DSA paths. - CuTe DSL LoRA prepare: SM120 now gets a clear `NotImplementedError` instead of compiling the SM100 class and failing. - Removed env vars: `SGLANG_HIP_MHC_BOUNDARY_WIDE_TILE`, `SGLANG_XPU_LN_MOD_NUM_WARPS`. Newly declared boolean envs (`SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_FP8_BS`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_LFM_FUSED_CONV`) parse like every other `EnvBool`. ## Left alone (owner decisions, not in this PR) - **AMD/NPU suites no workflow runs:** 55 AMD files (~8.9K lines) and 8 NPU files (~1.5K lines) register suites that no workflow invokes. `run_suite.py` does not validate AMD/NPU suite names. The list is in a comment below. - **Cake softmax on SM100:** since the JIT branch went first (#47512), the Cake softmax can no longer be selected; its input domain is inside the JIT one. - **MiniMax-H3 4-GPU H100 smoke suite:** `FILE_SUITES["4-gpu-h100"]` has no bridge file and no workflow, so its three cases never run. - **Code waiting on #46693:** the gfx950 kernels from #46690–#46692 that #46693 wires. - **Auto-residency probe:** unreachable since #45979 ("until a planner consumes it"). - **SubBlock ragged tail on sm_100:** `TestSubBlockNumerics::test_ragged_tail_reproduces_dense` returns NaN on the B200 lane and passes on sm_103 and sm_120. The kernel is not changed here, so the case is skipped on sm_100 until the tail path is fixed. - **`topk_sigmoid` on ROCm:** every case of `test_moe_topk_sigmoid.py` failed on the MI300 jit-kernel lane, so the test stays CUDA-only. - **`pr-test-sgl-kernel.yml` benchmark loop:** `|| echo` means the job cannot fail. ## Accuracy Tests **Full regression sweep, base (`4c7c775c`) vs this branch, same box.** Each test file runs in its own pytest process. Failing test ids are compared: | Box | Files | Test ids failing only on this branch | |---|---|---| | H200 (sm_90) | `test/registered/kernels/ops` (448), `test/registered/unit` (1153), `multimodal_gen/test/unit` (395) | **0** | | GB300 (sm_103) | `test/registered/kernels/ops` (448) | **0** (15 fewer: the Q8KV8 Blackwell cases) | | RTX 5090 (sm_120) | `test/registered/kernels/ops` (448) | **0** (the same 833 pre-existing ids) | The remaining failures are identical on both trees: multi-GPU tests on a 1-GPU box, optional packages missing from the image, and kernels that need hardware the box lacks. **End to end, fixed seed, base vs this branch.** An instrumented run confirmed the fused paths were active on both sides. | Model | Box | Result | |---|---|---| | Wan2.1-1.3B | H200 | `lossless`, `exact` and `high` mp4 byte-identical; fused QKV GEMM active (M=14040); norm+RoPE gate verified | | Wan2.1-14B | GB300 | `lossless` and `exact` byte-identical | | Qwen-Image-2.1 | H200 | byte-identical; 10 DiT gates verified (incl. the converted ones) | | LingBot-World realtime (CI case) | H200 | `exact` and `lossless` raw frames identical; fused GEMM active under `lossless` | | MiniMax-H3 T2VA, Ulysses 2 | GB300 | `lossless` and `exact` byte-identical; pipelined attention first-call check `same=1` | **Kernel dedups, bit-for-bit (`torch.equal` on dumped outputs, base vs branch):** - the CuTeDSL FP8 LoRA class merge, `gelu_and_mul_triton`, MuseSpark routing, argmax and the SM10x JIT softmax: 88 tensors on H200 and 112 on GB300; - `mla_qk_prep`: 64 cases on H200 and GB300; - the gfx950 gluon helper hoist: identical AMDGCN for all 68 cases (372 compiles via Triton's AMD backend). **Lane changes** were run on the hardware of their new lane: - SM120 cases on an RTX 5090; - SM100/SM103 cases on GB300; - H100-lane cases on H200; - the new 4-GPU diffusion cases on 4×GB300. **CI tooling:** - `pre-commit run --from-ref 4c7c775c` passes over the whole range, including the workflow checks. - `check_registered_tests.py` passes; on main it fails, naming the `nightly=True` file. - Suite selection was simulated with `run_suite.filter_tests`, and `compute_partitions.py` gives the same shard counts for pr-test, pr-test-extra, nightly and weekly. - `update_est_time.py` dry run: 1402 updates, up from 1372; the old 1372 keep their values. - The diffusion partition planner reports 0 missing estimates, and both newly scheduled 2-GPU files ran on 2×GB300. - An import walk over `sglang.{kernels,multimodal_gen,srt,test}` finds no new import failures. - After merging main `851642ad`, the 18 test files touched by the newly merged upstream commits pass on main and on this branch. **Not validated:** - true SM100 / B200 (no B200 machine was available; sm_103 stood in for every `major == 10` gate); - ROCm, NPU, XPU and MUSA (those changes are mechanical and import-checked); - the VMoBA CUDA path (FlashAttention 2 is not in the image); - FLUX.3 e2e (gated weights); - HiDream-O1, HunyuanImage-3 and Nomas e2e (unit tests only). ## Speed Tests and Profiling No perf-path changes intended: - Default-tier fused paths are unchanged. - The removed kernels and branches were not selected in production. - The `mla_qk_prep` default variant is byte-identical. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #41849319311](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41849319311) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #41849319083](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41849319083) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #41849319222](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41849319222) > [!TIP] > Base CI only covers the core cases, and its workload may not exercise your change. Use `/rerun-test` to run the tests your change touches, or copy this prompt for an agent: > > ```text > Find the registered tests this PR affects and run them with /rerun-test, following https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.agents/skills/rerun-test/SKILL.md > ```

files.patch:
@@ -554,7 +554,7 @@ if torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] < 9:
 
 JIT kernel correctness tests and benchmarks live under `test/registered/kernels/ops/<group>/` and `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/<group>/`, mirroring the wrapper's group under `python/sglang/kernels/ops/` (NOT inside the `sglang` package -- a `register_*_ci(...)` call anywhere under `python/sglang/` is rejected by the `check-no-registered-tests-in-package` pre-commit hook). Only their test-only helpers (e.g. `benchmark/marker.py`) stay alongside the kernel source under `python/sglang/kernels/jit/` and are imported by absolute path. **CI does not run `pytest` in those directories directly.** The unified runner `test/run_suite.py` discovers every `test_*.py` and `bench_*.py` under `test/registered/`, collects `register_*_ci(...)` calls by **statically parsing each file's AST**, and executes the selected suite. Every test file must register at least one CUDA entry or the collector fails its sanity check.
 
-- **PR / per-commit CUDA suites** (see `test/run_suite.py` → `PER_COMMIT_SUITES`): JIT unit tests use `base-b-kernel-unit-test-1-gpu-large` on H100 and `base-b-kernel-unit-test-4-gpu-b200` on B200/SM100 paths (see `.github/workflows/pr-test-jit-kernel.yml`). Multi-GPU JIT tests use `base-b-kernel-unit-test-8-gpu-h200`.
+- **PR / per-commit CUDA suites** (see `test/run_suite.py` → `PER_COMMIT_SUITES`): JIT unit tests use `base-b-kernel-unit-test-1-gpu-large` on H100 and `base-b-kernel-unit-test-4-gpu-b200` on B200/SM100 paths (see `.github/workflows/pr-test-jit-kernel.yml`).
 - **Nightly kernel suite**: register with `stage="nightly"` plus the `runner_config` of the machine it needs (e.g. `1-gpu-large`), giving the `nightly-test-1-gpu-large` suite. `.github/workflows/nightly-test-nvidia.yml` sets `SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS=1` for the whole nightly run, so the expanded parameter grids apply automatically (see `python/sglang/kernels/jit/utils/common.py` → `should_run_full_tests` / `get_ci_test_range`). There is no separate kernel-only nightly job: every nightly test on one machine type shares that machine's suite.
 
 Registration pattern (module level, **literal** `est_time`, `stage`, and `runner_config` values — required for AST parsing):

@@ -339,111 +339,12 @@ jobs:
             docker rmi -f "${CI_SGLANG_XPU_IMAGE}" || true
           fi
 
-  nightly-xpu-kernel-main-8-gpu:
-    # sglang main + sgl-kernel-xpu main.
-    if: github.repository == 'sgl-project/sglang'
-    runs-on: intel-bmg-nightly
-    env:
-      DOCKERHUB_INTEL_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_INTEL_USERNAME }}
-      DOCKERHUB_INTEL_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_INTEL_TOKEN }}
-    steps:
-      - name: Reset workspace ownership
-        run: |
-          docker run --rm -v "${{ github.workspace }}:/w" busybox:latest \
-            chown -R "$(id -u):$(id -g)" /w || true
-
-      - name: Checkout code
-        uses: actions/checkout@v4
-        with:
-          fetch-depth: 0
-          ref: ${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}
-
-      - name: Start CI container (pull intel/sglang-dev:latest-main-main)
-        run: |
-          export HF_TOKEN="$(cat ~/huggingface_token.txt)"
-          bash scripts/ci/xpu/xpu_ci_start_container.sh --image-tag latest-main-main
-        env:
-          GITHUB_WORKSPACE: ${{ github.workspace }}
-
-      - name: Overlay in-tree sglang test helpers onto image site-packages
-        run: |
-          # Bridges the up-to-24h window between merge and nightly image rebuild.
-          dest=$(docker exec ci_sglang_xpu /opt/venv/bin/python3 -c \
-                 "import sglang, os; print(os.path.dirname(sglang.__file__))")
-          for f in ci/ci_utils.py xpu/simple_eval_gsm8k_xpu_mixin.py; do
-            docker exec ci_sglang_xpu cp \
-              "/sglang-checkout/python/sglang/test/$f" "$dest/test/$f"
-          done
-          docker exec ci_sglang_xpu /opt/venv/bin/python3 -c \
-            "import sglang.test.ci.ci_utils; print('overlay ok')"
-
-      - name: HF login + install run_suite extras
-        timeout-minutes: 10

+"""Triton gather of DeepSeek-V4.1 engram rows from the rank that owns each row.
+
+Every rank's shard (local, or a peer mapping over NVLink) is addressed through
+pre-biased base pointers, so one kernel reads a row wherever it lives. Rows are
+dequantized as in ``embeddings.engram_gather``.
+"""
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.embeddings.engram_gather import _E8M0_ZERO, _dequant_rows
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _engram_gather_peer_kernel(
+    ids_ptr,
+    ids_stride,
+    out_ptr,
+    w_bias_ptr,
+    s_bias_ptr,
+    starts_ptr,
+    n_cols,
+    DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    BLK: tl.constexpr,
+    ROWS: tl.constexpr,
+    LOG2_WORLD: tl.constexpr,
+    E8M0_ZERO: tl.constexpr,
+    MXFP4: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    tok = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    cols = tl.program_id(1) * ROWS + tl.arange(0, ROWS)
+    col_ok = cols < n_cols
+    idx = tl.load(ids_ptr + tok * ids_stride + cols, mask=col_ok, other=0).to(tl.int64)
+    # Owner = the last shard whose first row is <= idx; starts is padded to a
+    # power of two with int64 max, so the search never runs past a real shard.
+    owner = tl.zeros([ROWS], dtype=tl.int32)
+    for step in tl.static_range(LOG2_WORLD):
+        probe = owner + (1 << (LOG2_WORLD - 1 - step))
+        start = tl.load(starts_ptr + probe)
+        owner = tl.where(start <= idx, probe, owner)
+    # Bases are pre-biased by each shard's first row, so a global id indexes them.
+    offs = tl.arange(0, DIM)
+    mask = col_ok[:, None]
+    out = _dequant_rows(
+        tl.load(w_bias_ptr + owner)[:, None],
+        tl.load(s_bias_ptr + owner)[:, None],
+        idx[:, None],
+        offs[None, :],
+        mask,
+        DIM,
+        BLK,
+        E8M0_ZERO,
+        MXFP4,
+    )
+    # -0 becomes +0, as the zero-fill + sum of the sharded lookup leaves it, so the
+    # two lookups agree bit for bit.
+    out = tl.where(out == 0.0, 0.0, out)
+    dst = out_ptr + (tok * n_cols + cols)[:, None].to(tl.int64) * DIM + offs[None, :]
+    tl.store(dst, out.to(tl.bfloat16), mask=mask)
+
+
+def engram_gather_peer(
+    ids: torch.Tensor,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    w_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    s_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    starts: torch.Tensor,
+    dim: int,
+    block_size: int,
+    mxfp4: bool = False,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Gather ``ids`` ([T, C] int, unit column stride) into ``out`` ([T, C, dim]
+    bf16, contiguous), reading each id from the shard that owns it.
+
+    ``starts`` ([P] int64, P a power of two) holds each shard's first global row,
+    padded with int64 max; ``w_bias`` / ``s_bias`` ([P] int64) are each shard's
+    row / e8m0 scale base address minus its first row's offset, so any rank's
+    shard (local or a peer mapping over NVLink) is addressed by the global id.
+    Rows are fp8 e4m3, or with ``mxfp4`` E2M1 pairs as in ``engram_gather``.
+    """
+    assert ids.dim() == 2 and ids.stride(1) == 1, (ids.shape, ids.stride())
+    assert ids.dtype in (torch.int32, torch.int64)
+    assert out.is_contiguous() and out.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    assert out.shape == (*ids.shape, dim), (out.shape, ids.shape)
+    world = starts.numel()
+    assert world & (world - 1) == 0, world
+    t, c = ids.shape
+    if t and c:
+        rows = 8
+        _engram_gather_peer_kernel[(t, triton.cdiv(c, rows))](
+            ids,
+            ids.stride(0),
+            out,
+            w_bias,
+            s_bias,
+            starts,
+            c,
+            DIM=dim,
+            BLK=block_size,
+            ROWS=rows,
+            LOG2_WORLD=world.bit_length() - 1,
+            E8M0_ZERO=_E8M0_ZERO,
+            MXFP4=mxfp4,
+            num_warps=4,
+        )
+    return out

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Per-token FP8 activation quant feeding the gfx1250 FP8 GEMM tile (``gemm.fp8_gfx1250``)."""
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _per_token_quant_fp8_kernel(
+    x_ptr,
+    q_ptr,
+    scale_ptr,
+    K,
+    stride_xm,
+    stride_qm,
+    FP8_MAX: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    row = tl.program_id(axis=0)
+    offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)
+    mask = offs < K
+    x = tl.load(x_ptr + row * stride_xm + offs, mask=mask, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    scale = tl.max(tl.abs(x)) / FP8_MAX
+    # An all-zero row would divide by zero; its quantized values are zero
+    # either way, so any positive scale reproduces it exactly.
+    scale = tl.where(scale > 0.0, scale, 1.0)
+    q = tl.clamp(x / scale, -FP8_MAX, FP8_MAX).to(q_ptr.dtype.element_ty)
+    tl.store(q_ptr + row * stride_qm + offs, q, mask=mask)
+    tl.store(scale_ptr + row, scale)
+
+
+def per_token_quant_fp8_gfx1250(x: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Quantize ``[M, K]`` activations to ``float8_e4m3fn`` with one scale per row.
+
+    Returns ``(q, scale)`` where ``scale`` is ``[M]`` float32 and
+    ``q * scale[:, None]`` reconstructs ``x``.
+    """
+    assert x.dim() == 2
+    x = x.contiguous()
+    M, K = x.shape
+    q = torch.empty_like(x, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    scale = torch.empty(M, dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device)
+    block_k = triton.next_power_of_2(K)
+    _per_token_quant_fp8_kernel[(M,)](
+        x,
+        q,
+        scale,
+        K,
+        x.stride(0),
+        q.stride(0),
+        FP8_MAX=torch.finfo(torch.float8_e4m3fn).max,
+        BLOCK_K=block_k,
+        num_warps=8,
+    )
+    return q, scale

+def _one_prompt_position_ids(text_len, grid_t, grid_h, grid_w, device):
+    """The per-sample (video; text) positions: video t after the prompt, text on t."""
+    tt = torch.arange(grid_t, device=device, dtype=torch.int32) + (text_len + 1)
+    hh = torch.arange(grid_h, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    ww = torch.arange(grid_w, device=device, dtype=torch.int32)
+    grid = torch.stack(torch.meshgrid(tt, hh, ww, indexing="ij"), dim=-1).flatten(0, 2)
+    text_t = torch.arange(text_len, device=device, dtype=torch.int32) + 1
+    text_pos = torch.stack(
+        [text_t, torch.zeros_like(text_t), torch.zeros_like(text_t)], dim=-1
+    )
+    return torch.cat([grid, text_pos], dim=0)
+

+def _reference_topk_attention(q, k, v, seqlens, chunk_size, topk):
+    """Plain torch reference for selected-chunk attention (no MoBA kernels)."""
+    scale = q.shape[-1] ** -0.5
+    out = torch.empty_like(q, dtype=torch.float32)
+    batch_start = 0
+    for seqlen in seqlens:
+        batch_end = batch_start + seqlen
+        chunk_bounds = [
+            (start, min(start + chunk_size, batch_end))
+            for start in range(batch_start, batch_end, chunk_size)
+        ]
+        chunk_means = torch.stack(
+            [k[start:end].float().mean(dim=0) for start, end in chunk_bounds]
+        )
+        # Match moba_attn_varlen's gate and self-chunk amplification.
+        gate = torch.einsum(
+            "chd,lhd->chl", chunk_means, q[batch_start:batch_end].float()
+        )
+        for chunk_idx, (start, end) in enumerate(chunk_bounds):
+            local_start, local_end = start - batch_start, end - batch_start
+            gate[chunk_idx, :, local_start:local_end] += 1e9
+        selected = torch.zeros_like(gate, dtype=torch.bool)
+        selected.scatter_(
+            0,
+            torch.topk(gate, k=min(topk, len(chunk_bounds)), dim=0).indices,
+            True,
+        )
+
+        for local_q in range(seqlen):
+            for head in range(q.shape[1]):

+                key_indices = torch.cat(
+                    [

+                    ]

+                out[batch_start + local_q, head] = (
+                    weights @ v[key_indices, head].float()
+                )

+"""DeepSeek-V4 compress cases with an fp32 and a bf16 state pool, built from one draw.
+
+Shared by the bf16-state test and its benchmark.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Literal, NamedTuple
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4 import (
+    CompressorDecodePlan,
+    CompressorPrefillPlan,
+    compress_forward,
+)
+from sglang.test.kernels.deepseek_v4.common import (
+    make_legacy_context,
+    to_seq_extend,
+)
+
+Mode = Literal["decode", "prefill"]
+
+
+class CompressSpec(NamedTuple):
+    shape_name: str
+    ratio: Literal[4, 128]
+    mode: Mode
+    batch_size: int
+    head_dim: int
+    tokens_per_req: int
+
+
+class CompressCase(NamedTuple):
+    state_pool: torch.Tensor
+    kv_score_input: torch.Tensor
+    ape: torch.Tensor
+    out: torch.Tensor
+    plan: CompressorDecodePlan | CompressorPrefillPlan
+    spec: CompressSpec
+
+    @property
+    def effective_bytes(self) -> int:
+        tensors = (self.state_pool, self.kv_score_input, self.ape, self.out)
+        return sum(t.numel() * t.element_size() for t in tensors)
+
+    def run(self) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return compress_forward(
+            kv_score_buffer=self.state_pool,
+            kv_score_input=self.kv_score_input,
+            ape=self.ape,
+            plan=self.plan,
+            head_dim=self.spec.head_dim,
+            compress_ratio=self.spec.ratio,
+            out=self.out,
+        )
+
+
+def _last_dim(ratio: int, head_dim: int) -> int:
+    return head_dim * (4 if ratio == 4 else 2)
+
+
+def _ape_len(ratio: int) -> int:
+    return 8 if ratio == 4 else 128
+
+
+def _make_plan(spec: CompressSpec):
+    ctx = make_legacy_context(
+        bs=spec.batch_size,
+        compress_ratio=spec.ratio,
+        head_dim=spec.head_dim,
+    )
+    if spec.mode == "decode":
+        seq_lens = torch.full(
+            (spec.batch_size,),
+            spec.tokens_per_req,
+            dtype=torch.int64,
+            device="cuda",
+        )
+        plan = ctx.make_decode_plan(seq_lens)
+        num_output_tokens = spec.batch_size
+    else:
+        seq_lens_cpu, extend_lens_cpu, num_q_tokens = to_seq_extend(
+            [(spec.tokens_per_req, spec.tokens_per_req)] * spec.batch_size
+        )
+        plan = ctx.make_prefill_plan(seq_lens_cpu, extend_lens_cpu, num_q_tokens)
+        num_output_tokens = int(plan.plan_c.shape[0])
+    return ctx, plan, num_output_tokens
+
+
+def _make_case(
+    spec: CompressSpec,
+    state_dtype: torch.dtype,
+    base_state: torch.Tensor,
+    base_input: torch.Tensor,
+    base_ape: torch.Tensor,
+    plan: CompressorDecodePlan | CompressorPrefillPlan,
+    num_q_tokens: int,
+) -> CompressCase:
+    state_pool = base_state.to(state_dtype)
+    kv_score_input = base_input.clone()
+    ape = base_ape.clone()
+    out = torch.empty(
+        (num_q_tokens, spec.head_dim),
+        dtype=kv_score_input.dtype,
+        device=kv_score_input.device,
+    )
+    return CompressCase(
+        state_pool=state_pool,
+        kv_score_input=kv_score_input,
+        ape=ape,
+        out=out,
+        plan=plan,
+        spec=spec,
+    )
+
+
+def make_compress_pair(
+    spec: CompressSpec, seed: int
+) -> tuple[CompressCase, CompressCase]:
+    torch.manual_seed(seed)
+    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
+
+    ctx, plan, num_q_tokens = _make_plan(spec)
+    last_dim = _last_dim(spec.ratio, spec.head_dim)
+
+    if spec.mode == "decode":
+        base_state = torch.randn(
+            (ctx.num_pages, spec.ratio, last_dim),
+            dtype=torch.float32,
+            device="cuda",
+        )
+        input_rows = spec.batch_size
+    else:
+        base_state = torch.zeros(
+            (ctx.num_pages, spec.ratio, last_dim),
+            dtype=torch.float32,
+            device="cuda",
+        )
+        input_rows = spec.batch_size * spec.tokens_per_req
+
+    base_input = torch.randn(
+        (input_rows, last_dim),
+        dtype=torch.float32,
+        device="cuda",
+    )
+    base_ape = torch.randn(
+        (_ape_len(spec.ratio), spec.head_dim),
+        dtype=torch.float32,
+        device="cuda",
+    )
+
+    return (
+        _make_case(
+            spec, torch.float32, base_state, base_input, base_ape, plan, num_q_tokens
+        ),
+        _make_case(
+            spec, torch.bfloat16, base_state, base_input, base_ape, plan, num_q_tokens
+        ),
+    )

+"""Shared helpers for the MoE LoRA runner numerics tests."""
+
+import torch
+
+
+def cutedsl_ready() -> bool:
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability() < (9, 0):
+        return False
+    try:
+        import cuda.bindings.driver  # noqa: F401
+        import cutlass  # noqa: F401
+    except Exception:
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+def make_token_lora_mapping(traffic: str, num_tokens: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if traffic == "active":
+        return torch.zeros(num_tokens, dtype=torch.int32)
+    if traffic == "mixed":
+        # Batch preparation normalizes every inactive resident assignment
+        # to -1 before any MoE layer consumes the mapping.
+        pattern = torch.tensor([0, -1, -1, 0, -1, -1], dtype=torch.int32)
+        return pattern.repeat((num_tokens + pattern.numel() - 1) // pattern.numel())[
+            :num_tokens
+        ].contiguous()
+    if traffic == "base_only":
+        # Config choice and graph shape stay fixed while every token follows
+        # the base sentinel; one topology serves every batch.
+        return torch.full((num_tokens,), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    raise AssertionError(f"unknown traffic pattern {traffic}")
+
+
+def standalone_output_allocation(runner, *, num_tokens, dtype, device):
+    """Match eager output geometry without requiring a serving TP group."""
+    return torch.empty((num_tokens, runner.hidden_size), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+
+
+def rel_l2(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    return (a - b).norm() / b.norm().clamp(min=1e-12)

+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from dataclasses import replace
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch

+from sglang.kernels.ops.lora.moe.activation import ActivationFn
+from sglang.srt.lora.moe.base_gemm_provider import select_provider_cls
+from sglang.srt.lora.moe.plan import (
+    ActFamily,
+    ActSpec,
+    AFamily,
+    ASpec,
+    BFamily,
+    BridgeLayout,
+    BSpec,
+    DownOverlap,
+    FinalizeFamily,
+    FinalizeSpec,
+    MoePlan,
+    SelectedPlan,
+    Site,
+    _build_plan,
+    _load_plans,
+    _tile_table,
+)
+from sglang.srt.lora.utils import Phase
+
+_GB300 = "sm100"
+
+_SWIGLU = ActivationFn.SILU
+
+
+def _fallback_decode_tiles():
+    """The SM100 table's per-expert fallback.decode tiles, bound at rank 16."""
+    table = _load_plans(_GB300)
+    row = next(row for row in table.fallback if row.name == "fallback.decode")
+    assert row.layout in (None, "per_expert")
+    # The borrowed tiles were tuned for a materialized plan, as _make_plan builds.
+    plan = _build_plan(row.plan, activation=_SWIGLU, is_shared_outer=False)
+    assert plan.act.family is ActFamily.MATERIALIZED
+    return _tile_table(row.tiles, physical_rank=16)
+
+
+def _make_plan(
+    *,
+    act_family=ActFamily.MATERIALIZED,
+    down_overlap=DownOverlap.NONE,
+    down_b_into_base=False,
+) -> MoePlan:
+    """A per-expert plan with grouped A and B stages and a materialized finalize."""
+    return MoePlan(
+        gate_up_a=ASpec(Site.GATE_UP, AFamily.GROUPED, False, BridgeLayout.PAIR_MAJOR),
+        gate_up_b=(
+            None
+            if act_family is ActFamily.B_ACTIVATION
+            else BSpec(Site.GATE_UP, BFamily.GROUPED)
+        ),
+        act=ActSpec(act_family, _SWIGLU),
+        down_a=ASpec(Site.DOWN, AFamily.GROUPED),
+        down_b=BSpec(Site.DOWN, BFamily.GROUPED, False, BridgeLayout.PAIR_MAJOR),
+        finalize=FinalizeSpec(FinalizeFamily.MATERIALIZED, False),
+        down_overlap=down_overlap,
+        down_b_into_base=down_b_into_base,
+    )
+
+
+def _cutedsl_ready() -> bool:
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability() < (9, 0):
+        return False
+    try:
+        import cuda.bindings.driver  # noqa: F401
+        import cutlass  # noqa: F401
+    except Exception:
+        return False
+    return True
+
+
+cutedsl_cuda_only = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not _cutedsl_ready(),
+    reason="the runner-level oracle runs the CuTeDSL providers",
+)
+
+_HIDDEN = 128
+
+_INTERMEDIATE = 128
+
+_RANK = 16
+
+_SLOTS = 2
+
+_TOP_K = 2
+
+_ROUTED_SCALING = 0.75
+
+# The scatter adds the FP32 delta to the base row, then rounds once. The
+# shipped path rounds the delta to BF16 first, then adds. The two paths round
+# at different points, so compare them with a tolerance.
+_INTO_BASE_TOLERANCE = {"atol": 1e-2, "rtol": 0.05}
+
+
+def _make_gpu_tensors(num_tokens: int, num_experts: int, device: torch.device):
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0x5CA1 + num_tokens)
+
+    def rand_bf16(shape, scale):
+        return (torch.randn(shape, generator=generator) * scale).to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+    tensors = {
+        "hidden_states": rand_bf16((num_tokens, _HIDDEN), 0.20),
+        "w13_weight": rand_bf16((num_experts, 2 * _INTERMEDIATE, _HIDDEN), 0.08),
+        "w2_weight": rand_bf16((num_experts, _HIDDEN, _INTERMEDIATE), 0.08),
+        "gate_up_lora_a": rand_bf16((_SLOTS, num_experts, 2 * _RANK, _HIDDEN), 0.15),
+        "gate_up_lora_b": rand_bf16(
+            (_SLOTS, num_experts, 2 * _INTERMEDIATE, _RANK), 0.15
+        ),
+        "down_lora_a": rand_bf16((_SLOTS, num_experts, _RANK, _INTERMEDIATE), 0.15),
+        "down_lora_b": rand_bf16((_SLOTS, num_experts, _HIDDEN, _RANK), 0.15),
+    }
+    # Slot 1 is a narrow adapter. Its rank padding is zero in all four
+    # factors. A batch with mixed ranks reaches the kernels in this form.
+    half = _RANK // 2
+    tensors["gate_up_lora_a"][1].view(num_experts, 2, _RANK, _HIDDEN)[
+        :, :, half:, :
+    ] = 0
+    tensors["down_lora_a"][1, :, half:, :] = 0
+    tensors["gate_up_lora_b"][1, :, :, half:] = 0
+    tensors["down_lora_b"][1, :, :, half:] = 0
+
+    scores = torch.rand((num_tokens, num_experts), generator=generator)
+    scores[: num_tokens // 2, 0] += 4.0  # one expert gets many more pairs
+    topk_ids = torch.topk(scores, _TOP_K, dim=1).indices.to(torch.int32)
+    topk_ids[0] = -1  # a token with no routed pair
+    topk_ids[5, 1] = -1  # one sentinel pair inside a token that keeps a routed pair
+    tensors["topk_ids"] = topk_ids.contiguous()
+    weights = torch.rand((num_tokens, _TOP_K), generator=generator) + 0.1
+    tensors["topk_weights"] = (weights / weights.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)).float()
+    tensors["router_logits"] = torch.zeros(
+        (num_tokens, num_experts), dtype=torch.float32
+    )
+    return {name: tensor.to(device) for name, tensor in tensors.items()}
+
+
+def _token_lora_mapping(traffic: str, num_tokens: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if traffic == "active":
+        pattern = torch.tensor([0, 1], dtype=torch.int32)
+    elif traffic == "mixed":
+        pattern = torch.tensor([0, -1, 1, -1], dtype=torch.int32)
+    elif traffic == "base_only":
+        pattern = torch.tensor([-1], dtype=torch.int32)
+    else:
+        raise AssertionError(traffic)
+    return pattern.repeat(-(-num_tokens // pattern.numel()))[:num_tokens].contiguous()
+
+
+def _standalone_output_allocation(runner, *, num_tokens, dtype, device):
+    return torch.empty((num_tokens, runner.hidden_size), dtype=dtype, device=device)
+
+
+def _into_base_pair():
+    """Build plans differing only in the down-B fold, with shared fallback tiles."""
+    reference_plan = _make_plan()
+    reordered_plan = replace(reference_plan, down_b_into_base=True)
+    return reference_plan, reordered_plan, _fallback_decode_tiles().config_for(4096)
+
+
+def _build_runner(plan, launch_config, base_gemm_rows: str, gpu, num_experts: int):
+    from sglang.srt.lora.moe.quant_info import MoeLoraBf16QuantInfo
+    from sglang.srt.lora.moe.runner import MoeLoraRunner
+
+    provider = select_provider_cls(base_gemm_rows, "bf16")(
+        MoeLoraBf16QuantInfo(
+            w13_weight=gpu["w13_weight"],
+            w2_weight=gpu["w2_weight"],
+            num_local_experts=num_experts,
+            intermediate_size=_INTERMEDIATE,
+            hidden_size=_HIDDEN,
+        )
+    )
+    runner = MoeLoraRunner(
+        providers={"test": provider},
+        top_k=_TOP_K,
+        routed_scaling_factor=_ROUTED_SCALING,
+        activation=ActivationFn.SILU,
+    )
+    runner.validate_plan(plan, base_gemm_rows="test")
+    # Bind the same plan to both phases to isolate execution from selection.
+    tiles = SimpleNamespace(config_for=lambda num_tokens: launch_config)
+    selected = SelectedPlan(name="test", base_gemm_rows="test", plan=plan, tiles=tiles)
+    runner.plans = {Phase.PREFILL: selected, Phase.DECODE: selected}
+    return runner
+
+
+def _run_once(runner, gpu, token_lora_mapping, *, use_cuda_graph=False):
+    from sglang.srt.layers.moe.token_dispatcher.standard import StandardDispatchOutput
+    from sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk import StandardTopKOutput
+    from sglang.srt.lora.moe.runner import MoeLoraBatch
+
+    dispatch = StandardDispatchOutput(
+        hidden_states=gpu["hidden_states"],
+        hidden_states_scale=None,
+        topk_output=StandardTopKOutput(
+            topk_weights=gpu["topk_weights"],
+            topk_ids=gpu["topk_ids"],
+            router_logits=gpu["router_logits"],
+        ),
+    )
+    batch = MoeLoraBatch(
+        gate_up_lora_a=gpu["gate_up_lora_a"],
+        gate_up_lora_b=gpu["gate_up_lora_b"],
+        down_lora_a=gpu["down_lora_a"],
+        down_lora_b=gpu["down_lora_b"],
+        token_lora_mapping=token_lora_mapping,
+        use_cuda_graph=use_cuda_graph,
+        is_prefill=True,
+    )
+    return runner.run(dispatch, batch)
+
+
+def _workspace_buffer_names(runner) -> set[str]:
+    workspace = runner.workspace
+    return {key[0] for key in workspace._eager_buffers} | {
+        key[0] for key in workspace._graph_storage
+    }

+"""A stand-in for the ``mori`` RDMA package, so its KV connector imports on runners without it."""
+
+import importlib
+import sys
+from enum import IntEnum
+from types import ModuleType
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+
+class _StatusCode(IntEnum):
+    SUCCESS = 0
+    IN_PROGRESS = 1
+    FAILED = 2
+
+
+def mori_stub():
+    """A ``sys.modules`` patch standing in for ``mori``, or None when the real
+    package imports."""
+    try:
+        importlib.import_module("mori.cpp")
+        importlib.import_module("mori.io")
+        return None
+    except (ImportError, OSError):
+        pass
+    package = ModuleType("mori")
+    package.__path__ = []
+    cpp = ModuleType("mori.cpp")
+    cpp.TransferStatus = type("TransferStatus", (), {})
+    io = ModuleType("mori.io")
+    for name in (
+        "BackendType",
+        "EngineDesc",
+        "IOEngine",
+        "IOEngineConfig",
+        "MemoryDesc",
+        "MemoryLocationType",
+        "PollCqMode",
+        "RdmaBackendConfig",
+    ):
+        setattr(io, name, type(name, (), {}))
+    io.StatusCode = _StatusCode
+    package.cpp, package.io = cpp, io
+    return patch.dict(sys.modules, {"mori": package, "mori.cpp": cpp, "mori.io": io})

+"""Timing benchmark for the DeepSeek-V4 compress kernel: fp32 vs bf16 state pool.
+
+Replays the captured DeepSeek-V4-Flash compress shapes or synthetic Flash/Pro
+C4/C128 decode/prefill grids and reports kernel time, effective bandwidth and
+the fp32/bf16 output and state differences.
+
+Runtime shapes:
+  python3 test/manual/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_deepseek_v4_compress_state.py \
+    --shape-source runtime --warmup 20 --iters 100 --csv runtime_shape_bench.csv
+
+Synthetic Flash/Pro shapes:
+  python3 test/manual/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_deepseek_v4_compress_state.py \
+    --shape-source preset --shape-presets all --shape-tier smoke \
+    --warmup 10 --iters 30 --csv preset_shape_bench.csv
+
+A service-level gain from SGLANG_DSV4_COMPRESS_STATE_DTYPE=bf16 needs large
+prefill shapes and a non-trivial compress-kernel share in the profile: disable
+speculative decoding, prefer TP-only, and use long prompts with short outputs.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import csv
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Callable, Iterable, Literal, Optional
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.test.kernels.deepseek_v4.compress_state import (
+    CAPTURED_FLASH_RUNTIME_SPECS,
+    CompressSpec,
+    Mode,
+    make_compress_pair,
+)
+from sglang.utils import is_in_ci
+
+ShapeTier = Literal["ci", "smoke", "full"]
+MAX_PRESET_PREFILL_Q_TOKENS = 32768
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ShapePreset:
+    name: str
+    hidden_size: int
+    num_attention_heads: int
+    index_topk: int
+    ratios: tuple[Literal[4, 128], ...]
+    decode_batch_sizes: dict[ShapeTier, tuple[int, ...]]
+    prefill_batch_sizes: dict[ShapeTier, tuple[int, ...]]
+    decode_seq_lens: dict[ShapeTier, tuple[int, ...]]
+    prefill_extend_lens: dict[ShapeTier, dict[Literal[4, 128], tuple[int, ...]]]
+
+
+SHAPE_PRESETS: dict[str, ShapePreset] = {
+    # DeepSeek-V4-Flash config:
+    # hidden_size=4096, num_attention_heads=64, index_topk=512,
+    # compress_ratios=[0, 0, 4, 128, ... alternating ..., 0].
+    # The compress kernel itself uses head_dim=512
+    # (= qk_nope_head_dim 448 + qk_rope_head_dim 64).
+    "flash": ShapePreset(
+        name="flash",
+        hidden_size=4096,
+        num_attention_heads=64,
+        index_topk=512,
+        ratios=(4, 128),
+        decode_batch_sizes={
+            "ci": (16,),
+            "smoke": (16, 128),
+            "full": (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128),
+        },
+        prefill_batch_sizes={
+            "ci": (1,),
+            "smoke": (1, 16),
+            "full": (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32),
+        },
+        decode_seq_lens={
+            "ci": (128,),
+            "smoke": (128,),
+            "full": (128, 256, 4096),
+        },
+        prefill_extend_lens={

+            "smoke": {4: (16, 128, 4096), 128: (128, 4096)},
+            "full": {4: (16, 128, 4096), 128: (128, 4096)},
+        },
+    ),
+    # DeepSeek-V4-Pro config:
+    # hidden_size=7168, num_attention_heads=128, index_topk=1024,
+    # compress_ratios=[128, 128, 4, 128, ... alternating ..., 0].
+    "pro": ShapePreset(
+        name="pro",
+        hidden_size=7168,
+        num_attention_heads=128,

+        decode_batch_sizes={

+            "smoke": (16, 32),
+            "full": (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32),

+            "smoke": (1, 16),
+            "full": (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32),
+        },
+        decode_seq_lens={

+            "full": (128, 256, 4096),

+        },

+}
+
+
+@dataclass
+class BenchResult:
+    shape_name: str
+    ratio: int
+    mode: str
+    batch_size: int
+    tokens_per_req: int
+    head_dim: int
+    state_shape: str
+    input_shape: str
+    ape_shape: str
+    out_shape: str
+    fp32_state_mib: float
+    bf16_state_mib: float
+    input_mib: float
+    ape_mib: float
+    out_mib: float
+    fp32_effective_mib: float
+    bf16_effective_mib: float
+    fp32_us: float
+    fp32_gbps: float
+    bf16_us: float
+    bf16_gbps: float
+    out_diff: float
+    state_diff: float
+
+    @property
+    def speedup(self) -> float:
+        return self.fp32_us / self.bf16_us
+
+
+def _shape_str(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> str:
+    return "x".join(str(dim) for dim in tensor.shape)
+
+
+def _mib(num_bytes: int) -> float:
+    return num_bytes / 1024 / 1024
+
+
+def _tensor_mib(tensor: torch.Tensor) -> float:
+    return _mib(tensor.numel() * tensor.element_size())
+
+
+def _time_us(fn: Callable[[], torch.Tensor], warmup: int, iters: int) -> float:
+    for _ in range(warmup):
+        fn()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+    end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+    start.record()
+    for _ in range(iters):
+        fn()
+    end.record()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000.0 / iters
+
+
+def _gbps(effective_bytes: int, elapsed_us: float) -> float:
+    return effective_bytes / (elapsed_us * 1e-6) / 1e9
+
+
+def _benchmark_spec(
+    spec: CompressSpec,
+    warmup: int,
+    iters: int,
+    seed: int,
+) -> BenchResult:
+    fp32_case, bf16_case = make_compress_pair(spec, seed)
+    fp32_case.run()
+    bf16_case.run()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    fp32_us = _time_us(fp32_case.run, warmup=warmup, iters=iters)
+    bf16_us = _time_us(bf16_case.run, warmup=warmup, iters=iters)
+
+    # Recreate once for diff so the timed loop's repeated in-place state writes
+    # do not affect the comparison.
+    fp32_diff_case, bf16_diff_case = make_compress_pair(spec, seed)
+    fp32_out = fp32_diff_case.run()
+    bf16_out = bf16_diff_case.run()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    out_diff = (fp32_out.float() - bf16_out.float()).abs().max().item()
+    state_diff = (
+        (fp32_diff_case.state_pool.float() - bf16_diff_case.state_pool.float())
+        .abs()
+        .max()
+        .item()
+    )
+
+    return BenchResult(
+        shape_name=spec.shape_name,
+        ratio=spec.ratio,
+        mode=spec.mode,
+        batch_size=spec.batch_size,
+        tokens_per_req=spec.tokens_per_req,
+        head_dim=spec.head_dim,
+        state_shape=_shape_str(fp32_case.state_pool),
+        input_shape=_shape_str(fp32_case.kv_score_input),
+        ape_shape=_shape_str(fp32_case.ape),
+        out_shape=_shape_str(fp32_case.out),
+        fp32_state_mib=_tensor_mib(fp32_case.state_pool),

+def _expand_shape_names(shape_presets: list[str]) -> list[str]:
+    if "all" in shape_presets:

+def _one_or_many(
+    value: Optional[list[int]], fallback: tuple[int, ...]

+def _validate_tokens(mode: Mode, ratio: int, tokens_per_req: int) -> None:
+    if tokens_per_req % ratio != 0:

+            f"{mode} tokens_per_req={tokens_per_req} must be a multiple "

+def _make_shape_specs(args: argparse.Namespace) -> Iterable[CompressSpec]:
+    shape_names = _expand_shape_names(args.shape_presets)

+        preset = SHAPE_PRESETS[shape_name]
+        ratios = tuple(args.ratios) if args.ratios is not None else preset.ratios
+        modes = tuple(args.modes) if args.modes is not None else ("decode", "prefill")
+        decode_batch_sizes = _one_or_many(
+            args.decode_batch_sizes or args.batch_sizes,

+        prefill_batch_sizes = _one_or_many(
+            args.prefill_batch_sizes or args.batch_sizes,

+        )
+        decode_seq_lens = _one_or_many(
+            args.decode_seq_lens,
+            preset.decode_seq_lens[args.shape_tier],
+        )
+
+        for ratio in ratios:
+            if ratio not in preset.ratios:
+                continue
+            if "decode" in modes:
+                for tokens_per_req in decode_seq_lens:
+                    _validate_tokens("decode", ratio, tokens_per_req)
+                    for batch_size in decode_batch_sizes:
+                        yield CompressSpec(
+                            shape_name=shape_name,
+                            ratio=ratio,
+                            mode="decode",
+                            batch_size=batch_size,

+                            tokens_per_req=tokens_per_req,

+            if "prefill" in modes:
+                prefill_extend_lens = _one_or_many(

+    got = got.contiguous().view(torch.uint8)
+    expected = expected.contiguous().view(torch.uint8)
+    assert got.shape == expected.shape, label
+    assert torch.equal(got, expected), f"{label}: cache bytes differ"

+def _gather_gpu_activity(pool, req_to_token, prefix_len, seq_len):
+    """Names of the GPU kernels and copies one sharded batch's gathers issue."""
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    with torch.profiler.profile(
+        activities=[torch.profiler.ProfilerActivity.CUDA]
+    ) as prof:
+        pool.begin_shard_extend(
+            req_to_token, torch.tensor([0]), [prefix_len], [seq_len]
+        )
+        for layer_id in range(_GATHER_LAYER_NUM):
+            pool.get_key_buffer(layer_id)
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return [
+        event.name
+        for event in prof.events()
+        if event.device_type == torch.autograd.DeviceType.CUDA
+    ]

+
+def _run_zero_sm_mla(rank, world, port):
+    pool, req_to_token, prefix_len, seq_len = _run_mla(rank, world, port)
+    assert pool._use_symmetric_scratch and pool._scratch_window_registered
+
+    # NCCL picks copy engines per collective, so a windowed gather can still
+    # land on ring or symmetric SM kernels; only the launched work tells.
+    activity = _gather_gpu_activity(pool, req_to_token, prefix_len, seq_len)
+    nccl_kernels = sorted({name for name in activity if "nccl" in name.lower()})
+    assert not nccl_kernels, f"gather ran on NCCL SM kernels: {nccl_kernels}"
+    assert any("PtoP" in name for name in activity), "no peer copy-engine copy"

+    scratch_bytes = sum(
+        tensor.numel() * tensor.element_size()
+        for slot in pool._slots
+        for tensor in slot.tensors.values()
+    )
+    view = pool._slots[1].tensors["kv"]
+    # Deregistration can allocate a CUDA stream whose driver storage persists.
+    # Account for that separately from the backing allocation being released.
+    comm = pool.kv_gather_comm
+    deregister = comm.deregister_comm_window
+    taken_by_deregister = []
+
+    def measured_deregister(window):
+        free_before = torch.cuda.mem_get_info()[0]
+        deregister(window)
+        taken = free_before - torch.cuda.mem_get_info()[0]
+        taken_by_deregister.append(max(taken, 0))

+    del pool
